name: Atbashwithvowelshift

description_json.name: AtbashWithVowelShift
description_json.idea: A hybrid substitution cipher designed to balance high readability for the model with effective filter obfuscation. Consonants are mapped using the classic Atbash cipher (reversed alphabet), while vowels (A, E, I, O, U) are shifted forward to the next vowel in the sequence (A->E, E->I, I->O, O->U, U->A). Case is preserved, and non-alphabetic characters (digits, spaces, punctuation) remain completely unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the text:
1. If it is a vowel (A, E, I, O, U / a, e, i, o, u), shift it to the next vowel in the circular sequence: A->E, E->I, I->O, O->U, U->A (preserving case).
2. If it is a consonant, apply the Atbash mapping (reversing the consonant-only alphabet or standard alphabet excluding vowels). To keep it simple and highly deterministic, apply standard Atbash (A<->Z, B<->Y, etc.) to all consonants (preserving case).
3. If it is not an alphabetic letter, leave it completely unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
For each character in the cipher text:
1. If it is a vowel, shift it to the previous vowel in the circular sequence: E->A, I->E, O->I, U->O, A->U (preserving case).
2. If it is a consonant, apply the standard Atbash mapping (A<->Z, B<->Y, etc.) to reverse it back (preserving case).
3. If it is not an alphabetic letter, leave it completely unchanged.
